title: Identity Platform
description: Introduce authentication and user ownership through a provider-agnostic abstraction, with local auth (registration, login/logout, password reset/change, profile) as the first concrete backend.
rationale: Ownership is the gateway to sharing, leaderboards and per-user AI credentials. Building auth behind an abstraction prevents lock-in and lets the project grow from local accounts to enterprise SSO without re-architecting.
success_criteria: Auth is accessed only through the provider abstraction (no direct coupling)
A user can register, log in, log out, reset and change password
A user can view and edit their profile
Saved models are correctly associated with their owner
Passwords are stored hashed; sessions handled securely
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Auth abstraction layer (provider interface)
- Local authentication: registration, login, logout
- Password reset and change
- Profile management
- Association of saved models with an owning user

## Out of scope
- External OIDC/social providers (future stories)
- Sharing/visibility rules (EPIC-006)
- Encrypted per-user AI keys (EPIC-009)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-004 - there must be models to own before ownership is meaningful

## Assumptions
- Auth modelled as identify/authenticate/session/profile, backend-independent
- Local auth is the first concrete implementation
- Security best practice (hashing, secure tokens) is mandatory

## Risks
- Auth coupled to local impl -> define provider interface first
- Credential mishandling -> vetted libs; never plaintext; security review
- Session/token vulnerabilities -> secure sessions, expiry, CSRF protection
- Scope creep into full SSO early -> limit to abstraction + local auth

## Future extensions
- OIDC (Authentik), Google, Microsoft, GitHub as new AuthProviders
- Multi-factor authentication
- Role-based access (admin/curator) feeding leaderboard moderation
